السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته،

نحن فريق “Youthful minds, futures guide” طالبات بجامعة الملك عبدالعزيز، مجموعه شغوفه بالفضاء وعلومه ونطمح لأن نكون خير رمز لشباب جبل طويق ونبني اثراً وطريقاً للمستقبل.

فريقناً مكون من كل من تخصص الفيزياء، علوم الحاسب، والاحصاء، ونبحث عن متخصصين شغوفين بتصميم الجرافيك، إدارة الاعمال، أو التسويق

بمهارات سردية والتمكن في تقديم وانشاء العروض الترويجيه لفكرة المشروع، ان كانت احد هذه المتطلبات تنطبق عليكِ نسعد بإنضمامك لفريقنا.
summary:
Fire behaves fundamentally differently in microgravity than on Earth, forming spherical, low-soot flames driven by diffusion rather than buoyant convection. Understanding this phenomenon is critical for crew safety and spacecraft material selection, yet.. raw data from space combustion experiments can be complex and difficult to interpret quickly and here is where the role of our idea comes.

 IVSFE (Interactive Visual Display Panel for Spacecraft Fire Experiments) is an intuitive, data-driven visual interface designed to bridge this gap. By integrating open-access microgravity combustion datasets from NASA (such as the Saffire-2(PSI-99), and BASS-2(PSI-25)
experiments), IVSFE transforms complex telemetry, thermal profiles, and flame spread metrics into interactive, real-time visualizations.
 Our platform enables researchers, engineers, students, and mostly astronauts to explore, compare, and analyze how different materials ignite and burn in zero gravity. Through dynamic charts and visual simulations, IVSFE enhances situational awareness for spacecraft fire safety protocols and democratizes access to NASA’s vital combustion research.

AI or “SI” usage disclosure

Programming stage

Code Debugging & Optimization: Fixed syntax and runtime errors (such as duplicate chart rendering and variable reference issues), indentation errors while preserving the original clean code structure.

Interactive Controls & Logic: Assisted with setting up the range sliders so they pull their default values from the dataset, and helped adjust the conditional logic to trigger the right safety warnings.

Hosting & Deployment: Helped troubleshoot connection issues when testing the app on mobile, and guided me through setting up the required project files to deploy the dashboard online via GitHub.

Data sample providing stage

NASA PSI Data Navigation: Guided the navigation of NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository to locate relevant combustion datasets (SAFFIRE-II and BASS-II).

Data Cleaning & Terminology Clarification: Clarified NASA experimental terminology and abbreviations (e.g., pot, ign, blowoff, ext) and assisted in structuring a clean, unified CSV dataset.

Physics Action Synthesis: Assisted in drafting concise English physics explanations that link experimental extinction data with official NASA SAFFIRE-II documentation notes.

NOTE:

ALL DATA, NUMBERS, AND CODES WERE

EXTRACTED, REVIEWED AND VERIFIED

MANUALLY BY TEAM MEMBERS FROM NASA'S

OFFICIAL REPOSITORIES, AND THE ROLE OF

ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE WAS LIMITED TO

ORGANISATION, ILLUSTRATION, AND

LANGUAGE DRAFTING.
